new_scholarship.name: CyprusAid Scholarship Scheme (Cyprus University of Technology) - Undergraduate
new_scholarship.official_source: Cyprus University of Technology, in collaboration with the 'CyprusAid' programme of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Cyprus
new_scholarship.duration: 4 years for the BSc in Nursing (after a one-year preparatory Greek-language course); 3 years for the two Higher Diploma programmes; the standing University terms allow extension of scholarship holders up to 6 years to complete the degree
new_scholarship.application_period: The 2026 cycle covered studies commencing in September 2026 and closed on Friday 12 June 2026; the call was published on 05/03/2026. The scheme is re-published annually, so a comparable window is expected in the first half of 2027 for September 2027 entry, but no 2027 call has been published.
new_scholarship.application_method: Separate application, not automatic on admission. Applications are submitted through the CUT bachelor programmes admissions online application page, selecting Application Type "Scholarships 'CyprusAid' (UND)" (or "Scholarships 'CyprusAid' (PHD)" for doctoral applicants).
new_scholarship.description: The Cyprus University of Technology, together with the 'CyprusAid' programme of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Cyprus, awards fully-tuition-funded scholarships for September 2026 study to nationals and permanent residents of a specified list of 36 countries, mainly African, Asian and Pacific states. At undergraduate level the scheme covers the BSc in Nursing and the Higher Diploma in Culinary Arts and the Higher Diploma in Hotel and Tourism Management. Successful candidates receive full tuition coverage, university dormitory accommodation, a monthly stipend of EUR 400, a laptop up to EUR 500, an air ticket to their home country up to EUR 1,000, permit and medical costs, and miscellaneous expenses up to EUR 100. This is not a worldwide international scholarship: applicants must hold the nationality of, and be permanent residents of, one of the listed eligible countries.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Secondary-school leavers who hold the nationality of one of the 36 listed eligible countries and are permanent residents of that same country, and who will study the BSc in Nursing, the Higher Diploma in Culinary Arts, or the Higher Diploma in Hotel and Tourism Management in September 2026.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Restricted by nationality and residence, not open to all international applicants. Applicants must hold a valid passport or ID card proving nationality of one of the listed eligible countries (Sao Tome and Principe, Armenia, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Lesotho, Eswatini, Liberia, Timor-Leste, Philippines, Indonesia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, South Africa, Ghana, Egypt, Lebanon, Palestine, Jordan, Bahrain, Ethiopia, Madagascar, Mauritius, Seychelles, the Comoros, Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Nauru, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu) and must be permanent residents of one of those eligible countries. Undergraduate applicants must also hold a Leaving Certificate from Secondary Education issued in one of the eligible countries and provide a certificate demonstrating English proficiency. Only three undergraduate programmes are covered, and two of the three are three-year Higher Diploma programmes rather than bachelor's degrees.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: The call publishes no ranking criteria, weighting, interview stage or number of awards. Outcome is notified electronically to the email address given in the application and through the University's Online Portal. The BSc in Nursing track is taught in Greek, so selection there depends on completing the preparatory Greek-language year; the two Paphos Higher Diploma programmes are taught in English.
new_scholarship.notes: Awarding body is the University together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' CyprusAid programme; the row is assigned to cut.ac.cy, which is the host publishing the call and administering applications. Three undergraduate programmes are covered but only the BSc in Nursing is a bachelor's degree (4 years, taught in Greek, with a preparatory Greek-language year); the Higher Diploma in Culinary Arts and the Higher Diploma in Hotel and Tourism Management are 3-year English-taught programmes at the Paphos campus that lead to a Higher Diploma, not a bachelor's award. The 2026 deadline (12 June 2026) has passed, so status is closed; the scheme is annual. CUT's published non-EU bachelor's tuition is EUR 6,834 per year (EU/Cypriot: EUR 3,417, paid by the government), published as a flat annual rate with no academic year attached on the fees page, plus a one-time EUR 40 registration fee for every new student that the scholarship does not list; the call itself names no currency or amount for its tuition coverage, so the funding figure recorded is the EUR 400 monthly stipend. fully_funded is set false in the detail block because the benefit package has published conditions and caps (stipend and dormitory rent withheld for July and/or August if the holder returns home, airfare capped at EUR 1,000, per-item caps) rather than an unconditional all-in award. The standing University Council decision of 24.9.2020 for scholarship students from Africa states a lower living allowance of EUR 300 per month and up to 6 years of duration; the 2026 call supersedes it for this cycle with EUR 400 per month.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: September 2026 entry; call published 05/03/2026, applications closed 12 June 2026
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: The call states a single deadline of Friday 12 June 2026 and no separate institutional or programme deadline. No clock time is published anywhere on the page, so the date is recorded without a time component and read in the University's local timezone (Europe/Nicosia, EEST/EET). Because 12 June 2026 precedes the verification date of 2026-10-03, this cycle is closed; the scheme is re-published annually, so a comparable mid-June deadline is expected for a September 2027 cycle but no such call is published yet.
programme_detail_official.status_note: The 2026 call is closed: its stated deadline of Friday 12 June 2026 has passed. The 2026 awards were for studies commencing in September 2026. The CyprusAid scheme is published annually by the University, so the next cycle is expected to open in the first half of 2027 with a deadline of roughly mid-June 2027 for September 2027 studies; that cycle has not been published, and no award places are currently open.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: For the full duration of studies: 4 years for the BSc in Nursing (after the one-year preparatory Greek-language course, which the scholarship terms also cover) and 3 years for the Higher Diploma in Culinary Arts and the Higher Diploma in Hotel and Tourism Management. The University's standing terms for scholarship students allow extension for up to 6 years where needed to complete the degree.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: The call states "Full tuition coverage" as benefit item 1 for all covered programmes. CUT's published fee schedule for Bachelor's programmes is EUR 6,834 annually for students from non-EU countries and EUR 3,417 annually for Cypriot and EU-member-state students (the latter paid by the government of the Republic of Cyprus); every eligible CyprusAid holder is a non-EU national who would otherwise be charged the EUR 6,834 figure, so "full tuition coverage" is read as waiving that published annual fee, though the call never states a currency or amount for the coverage itself. The EUR 6,834 figure is published as a flat annual bachelor's rate without an explicit academic-year label on the fees page, so the academic year it applies to is unstated and it is subject to periodic revision. fully_funded is nevertheless false: the package is capped and conditional rather than all-in. The living allowance is not paid for July and/or August if the holder returns to their home country, dormitory rent is not paid for those summer months in the standing terms, airfare to the home country is capped at EUR 1,000, and the insurance, medical examination and miscellaneous items are individually capped. The University also states that scholarship students are not charged tuition fees and that it does not ask the state to pay their tuition. The one-time EUR 40 registration fee payable by every new student in any programme is not among the scholarship benefits. No bond, return-of-service obligation or repayment condition is stated in the published terms for this award.

programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: International applicants only in the sense that they are non-Cypriot students from the listed countries; the scheme is not a worldwide international scholarship and excludes EU, Cypriot, UK, North American and other applicants whose nationality is not on the list. Every listed eligible country is outside the EU, and CUT's fee schedule confirms that EU-member-state citizens have their Greek-taught undergraduate tuition paid by the government of the Republic of Cyprus while students from non-EU countries pay tuition fees for all study programmes, so the scheme targets the non-EU group that would otherwise be charged tuition.

The same page does publish real figures, but for the doctoral track only - IELTS 6.5, or TOEFL 580 paper-based / 72 internet-based, or a G.C.E/I.G.C.S.E O level grade of C minimum - so those numbers must not be read as applying to this bachelor's-level application. In practice the two Paphos Higher Diploma programmes are taught in English, while the BSc in Nursing is taught in Greek.

supplements_or_initiatives: Related standing award: the University Council decision of 24.9.2020 (109th meeting) on scholarships for undergraduate students from Africa, under which the award includes a preliminary Greek-language year, lasts 4 years extendable to 6, and carries a living allowance of EUR 3,600 per year (EUR 300 x 12) plus dormitory rent up to EUR 3,000 (EUR 250 x 12) and an air ticket up to EUR 1,000. The 2026 call states a higher monthly allowance of EUR 400 and is the current figure for this cycle.

Related standing award: in collaboration with the Christian Orthodox Church of Kenya the University offers a full scholarship to a small number of students from Kenya and Uganda studying Nursing and other undergraduate programmes, with a preparatory Greek-language year.
programme_detail_official.description: The Cyprus University of Technology, in collaboration with the 'CyprusAid' programme of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Cyprus, offers scholarships for September 2026 study to nationals and permanent residents of 36 listed countries, mainly African, Asian and Pacific states. At undergraduate level the scheme covers the 4-year BSc in Nursing, which is taught in Greek and preceded by a covered one-year Greek-language course, and the 3-year, English-taught Higher Diploma in Culinary Arts and Higher Diploma in Hotel and Tourism Management at the Paphos campus. Successful candidates receive full tuition coverage, university dormitory accommodation, a monthly stipend of EUR 400, a laptop up to EUR 500, an air ticket to their home country up to EUR 1,000, Cyprus entry and residence permit fees with the associated compulsory medical examinations, an insurance contract up to EUR 180, and miscellaneous expenses up to EUR 100. Applications were made through the University's bachelor admissions portal under Application Type "Scholarships 'CyprusAid' (UND)" and closed on 12 June 2026.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Full tuition for the covered programme; university dormitory accommodation for the full duration of studies; EUR 400 monthly living allowance; laptop up to EUR 500; Cyprus entry permit application fee and compulsory medical examinations up to EUR 150; airfare to the home country up to EUR 1,000; residence permit application fee and compulsory medical examinations up to EUR 150; mandatory public-hospital health certificate; individual insurance contract up to EUR 180; special medical examinations up to EUR 180; miscellaneous expenses up to EUR 100; one-year preparatory Greek-language course for the BSc in Nursing.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality is on the published list of 36 eligible countries; if it is not, do not apply, because eligibility is by nationality and not merely by residence.
Confirm you are a permanent resident of one of the eligible countries and can evidence it, as the scheme requires both nationality and permanent residence.
Confirm you hold a Leaving Certificate from Secondary Education issued in one of the eligible countries.
Choose an eligible programme only: BSc in Nursing (Limassol, Greek-taught), Higher Diploma in Culinary Arts or Higher Diploma in Hotel and Tourism Management (Paphos, English-taught).
Obtain an English proficiency certificate even though no score is published for the undergraduate track, as a certificate is a stated requirement.
If applying to the BSc in Nursing, budget for and commit to the one-year preparatory Greek-language course at the CUT Language Centre in Limassol before the degree starts.
Prepare the Cyprus entry permit process early, since entry and residence permit application fees and compulsory medical examinations are covered but the process itself must be completed in time.
Watch for the next annual call; the scheme is re-published each cycle and the 2026 round has closed.
common_rejection_risks: Applying from a country that is not on the eligible list, or holding citizenship of an eligible country but permanent residence elsewhere.
Applying to a CUT undergraduate programme that is not one of the three covered programmes.
Expecting an IELTS or TOEFL score: none is published for the undergraduate track, so submitting only a school certificate without a proficiency certificate leaves a stated requirement unmet.
Missing the 12 June deadline, which applies to the scholarship application itself and not just to the admission application.
Not selecting Application Type "Scholarships 'CyprusAid' (UND)" in the portal, which would make the request an ordinary admission application rather than a scholarship request.
Assuming worldwide eligibility - the majority of international applicants, including all EU and English-speaking applicants, are excluded.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The EUR 40 registration fee payable by every new student in any programme at CUT is not listed among the scholarship benefits.
Living expenses in excess of the dormitory accommodation and the EUR 400 monthly allowance, including personal spending, are not covered by any published item.
Any July and August costs incurred while staying in Cyprus, since the allowance and dormitory rent are withheld if the holder returns home.
Costs exceeding the stated caps: airfare above EUR 1,000, laptop above EUR 500, insurance above EUR 180, and miscellaneous expenses above EUR 100.
Additional airfare beyond the single trip to the home country covered up to EUR 1,000.
Textbooks, course materials and travel between the Limassol and Paphos campuses, none of which appear in the published benefit list.
document_audit: Official certificate of citizenship, with copies of both the ID card and the valid passport.
Leaving Certificate from Secondary Education issued in one of the eligible countries.
Check that the name on every document matches the name used in the online application, since nationality and residence documents are matched against the eligible-country list.
For the BSc in Nursing, keep the completion record of the preparatory Greek-language year, as the scholarship terms cover that year separately.

The chosen PNG was probed on the institution's own registrable domain and returned an image content type with non-zero image bytes rather than an HTML WAF page, satisfying rule 5 and rule 7. The University also publishes a 'Digital Logo Files' brand page at /university/administration/administrative-services/Communication%2C+Marketing+and+International+Relations+Services/logo/digital_logo_files/, which was not needed once the header asset was confirmed. Note the host key is www.cut.ac.cy versus the assigned host cut.ac.cy, and the footer white logo is explicitly not used.
